(Shogo's route only)
Shogo is an unremarkable young man entering his third year of working in the planning department at Hihaku Soaps, a chemicals company headquartered in Sumida.

Born in western Tokyo to an ordinary family around the same time as the birth of color TV, he grew up amidst the boom of special effects-heavy action films, anime, variety shows, professional baseball, and pop music. Shogo graduated from a famous private university in Tokyo, and has since settled into an apolitical mindset —common among those of his generation— with no strong ideas and no particular dissatisfaction with the world as it develops around him. He is content to just go with the flow, having stumbled into his current position by pure chance, and it is safe to assume he will follow the stereotypical path of working his way up the ladder, starting a family, and remaining at the same company until retirement.
He plays folk guitar as a hobby and is currently looking for a girlfriend.
From in-game Persons of Interest profile

Shogo is a descendant of Tsuchimikado Seiman, making him a distant cousin of Hajime Yoshimi and Michiyo Shiraishi. Additionally, Shogo was unknowingly born with great spirit sense, making him the perfect candidate to summon Seiman's spirit (the Player) into present day.
After the events of The Seven Mysteries of Honjo, Shogo gained tremendous spirit sense and took over the role of Suigen Gamyodo after the original, Natsue Yamamori, retired.

Everything else about him remains a mystery.
From in-game Persons of Interest profile

The current chief of Paranormal Affairs is a man named Kuiru Nakagoshi. He was born to a family of psychics who have been involved in keeping the world safe from paranormal phenomena for generations, and has served as Mio Kurosuzu's mentor since discovering her. Kuiru is an elusive figure — very few have met him in person, and he is rarely seen in his office. It is said that this is because he has oft been the target of curses, however some theorize that it is in fact because Kuiru is not actually of flesh and blood at all. His seat in his office is usually occupied by a nue, a legendary creature found in Japanese folklore. The nue resembles an ordinary White's thrush and acts as Kuiru's messenger, leading to bizarre scenes of police officers earnestly reporting their findings to a bird.
The term "Nakagoshi case" serves as a code name used to refer to cases under investigation by Paranormal Affairs.
From in-game Files entry
Sex: Male
Occupation: Apprentice Ama Diver
Age: 18 years old

A young man born and raised on Kameshima. Although generally quiet and serious, he has an eccentric side that often sees him make jokes and wisecracks with a straight face, catching whoever he's talking to off guard.
In truth, he died five years ago in the disaster that occurred off Kameshima and was resurrected by a mermaid, becoming an 800-year immortal.

After losing his parents in the large-scale maritime accident five years ago, he was raised by his grandmother, veteran ama diver Tsuyu Minakuchi. He briefly found work at a seafood processing plant in Toba after graduating high school earlier in the year, but upon hearing that Tsuyu had injured her leg, forcing her to retire from diving and causing difficulties in her daily life, he quit his job after only three months and returned to Kameshima.

At present, he is caring for Tsuyu while looking for work on Kameshima, and he has recently made the decision to follow in Tsuyu's footsteps and become an ama diver himself. Although he has been unable to bring himself to enter the sea since the disaster five years ago, he is hoping that his previous aptitude for swimming will lend itself to a natural talent for ama diving.

Quiet and introverted as a child, he began to show a more animated side upon befriending Azami Kumoi, a boy his same age, and it eventually became a common sight to see them getting up to mischief together.

Although the maritime disaster five years ago saw a drastic shift in the way most of Kameshima's inhabitants treated Yuza, Azami alone continued to treat him the same. Even now, it is not uncommon for Azami to find himself caught up in Yuza's eccentric exploits, but he is always quick to laugh and follow his lead.
From in-game profile
His true age is 18, but his body remains that of a 13 year old boy.
Sex: Female
Occupation: Houseguest
Age: 17 years old
A mysterious girl currently lodging with Shinobu Wakamura, a local Kameshima magnate.
She became immortal after eating the flesh of a mermaid at some point in the past.
She was originally a maidservant working at the Bureau of Onmyo during the Heian period 800 years prior, where she was forced to eat mermaid flesh by Taira no Tomoshige.

Roughly three months ago, Sato suddenly arrived on Kameshima claiming that she was the child of a relative of the Wakamuras. She showed no sign of attending school or doing any sort of work, instead spending her days holed up in the Wakamura household, leading many islanders to wonder just who she is and what she's doing there.

Those who know about Wakamura's high-interest moneylending behind the scenes speculate that she might be the daughter of one of his borrowers, sent to work as a domestic servant to pay off a debt, but Sato herself is extremely easygoing and doesn't seem to be bothered by the endless rumors.

A huge television fan, she spends much of her spare time glued to the set in the Wakamura household, with her most recent obsessions being soap operas and two-hour thrillers. However, she isn't all that fond of period dramas.
She is good friends with Tsukasa Awao, who is close to her in age, and the two can often be seen enjoying themselves wandering the island together.
From in-game profile
Sato's true identity is Osato of Kusawa, and she is both the mythical Yao Bikuni of Ano Town from the Heian period and the historical Princess Hatsune from the Sengoku period.
Her true age is 817, but her body remains that of a 17 year old girl.

Occupation: Ittensai Shiki's Wife; Paranormal Affairs Employee
Age: Secret
A housewife from Tokyo who came to Kameshima to visit Wakamura.

A woman who balances her work as a housewife with her position as a full-time employee of the Paranormal Affairs Bureau, a secret department within the Tokyo Metropolitan Police. Although the very image of a refined lady in appearance, she has a surprisingly free-spirited personality and tends to find anything she has no interest in too bothersome to take seriously. Things that do catch her attention, on the other hand, often command all of it, and she will actively involve herself in looking into them.
She utterly adores her husband, swooning in admiration whenever the topic turns to him, and she is also viewed with affection by her coworkers, who call her "ma'am."

Out of the five current full-time members of the Paranormal Affairs Bureau, Yumeko alone lacks any particular metaphysical abilities despite possessing a meager degree of spirit sense. Even so, she was chosen to be part of the Bureau's elite unit for very particular reasons — reasons known only to a handful of people close to her.

There was once one other member of the Bureau who had no paranormal powers to speak of —veteran police detective Tetsuo Tsutsumi— and the two occasionally worked on investigations together. When dispatched on assignments now, she always pairs up with freelance psychic detective Sodo Kiryu, leaving all paranormal-related procedures —and often her much-despised paperwork— to him.
Yumeko's husband is also a psychic by the name of Ittensai Shiki, and Sodo is his cherished protégé.

Yumeko was formerly a mermaid by the name of Nagame. Unlike her more serious compatriots, Hayase and Sobae, Nagame was free-spirited by nature and held a keen interest in both humans and the mortal world. She was even known to break the rules to sneak out and observe human society — something which often put her at odds with the other two mermaids and led to her being viewed as something of a maverick.

When the entrance to Ryugu was sealed 400 years ago to suppress the Curse of the Raging Waves —rendering the remaining mermaids unable to return home— Sobae was overcome by grief; however, Nagame was thrilled, and seized the opportunity to travel the world at her leisure, which deepened the rift between her and Sobae.

For the next 350 years, Nagame bore witness to the lives of countless humans around the globe, from every culture and era, and her yearning for life in human society continued to grow. She was particularly enamored by the concepts of marriage and becoming a bride, finding the idea of pledging one's life to someone and living hand-in-hand with them from then on enthralling — it was this she found herself longing for above all else.

Nagame the mermaid became Ittensai Shiki's human wife, Yumeko Shiki, a name given to her by Ittensai himself. Although the process of gaining a human body meant she lost many of the memories and abilities she had possessed during her time as a mermaid, she retained all the memories and feelings from her time spent with Ittensai, which was more than enough for Yumeko.

Since then, Yumeko has enjoyed a fulfilling life, with her human nature —and her relationship with Ittensai— bringing her immense joy. Because of this, she is insistent that her primary identity be that of a housewife, to the extent that she always chooses clothing that will allow her return to tackling housework at a moment's notice.

However, the human body she has gained still differs from those of regular humans: although she appears to age slowly compared to those around her, it is entirely unknown how long her lifespan will end up being.

Following her rebirth as a human, Yumeko decided to pay a visit to Sobae in the depths of Ise Bay to explain her decision and introduce her partner. Abandoning her form as a mermaid to become human was a grave violation of the rules they were bound to, and she expected Sobae to receive the news with utter contempt if not sever her ties with Yumeko completely. But her expectations were pleasantly subverted: Sobae herself had since forged her own deep bond of love and trust with Mare Minakuchi —one that similarly transcended their respective species— and understood her feelings, thanking her for introducing Ittensai to her. However, Sobae never showed herself to Yumeko again after that.

Occupation: Author/Occult Journalist
Age: 40 years old

Nickname: "Avi." A fantasy author and occult journalist whose books are published in both America and England (but they apparently don't sell well). Unmarried. He has apparently come to Japan in search of mermaids.
Notable works include "The Fiend of Ringgit and the Solar Crow," "Hermod's Travels," and the "Bon Appétit, the Phantom Gourmand" series.

Although a grown man, he still has a certain naive boyishness to him, most evident in his passion for romantic tales and appetite for chasing his dreams. However, this also comes with an equivalent amount of immaturity, making him somewhat troublesome to deal with.

He believes that most any circumstance he finds himself in will sort itself out, an optimistic creed that often sees him casually throwing himself into difficult situations, and he remains impressively unbothered even on those occasions he does find himself in trouble, often managing to slip out of danger with nary a dent in his usual carefree attitude. That he's made it this far unscathed is largely owed to sheer luck, although he remains blissfully unaware of this.

He is currently in Japan seeking mermaid flesh, which is believed to grant immortality. His reason is simple: a fascination with the occult, a pursuit he feels is worthy of devoting his entire life to. Indeed, he is primarily driven by his pursuit of romantic ideals—if he finds something suitably inspiring, he will readily risk his life for it, and is willing to change his views just as quickly for the same.

Avi's interest in the occult was born when he discovered his great-grandmother's vast collection of mysterious occult artifacts in the storage of his family home in America. Among them was a mermaid mummy, which yielded a mysterious map when taken apart—a discovery which captivated his imagination and led to his current quest.

This great-grandmother happened to be a relative of the main Lunarlight family in England, albeit one who had chosen not to succeed the family estate. After discovering this through independent research into his lineage, Avi made contact with the Lunarlight family, and continues to maintain a secret correspondence with them to this day.
From in-game profile
Sex: Male
Occupation: Fisherman
Age: 19 years old

A young man born and raised on Kameshima, he has been friends with Yuza Minakuchi since childhood. He has a friendly and caring personality, and his willingness to help those around him has made him someone islanders of all ages rely on in times of need.

His father was a fisherman, and he accompanied him out to sea on his boat from a very young age. As a result, he grew up never doubting that he, too, would one day become a fisherman. After his father died in a maritime disaster five years ago, his mother —an ama diver— took on the responsibility of raising Azami and his much younger brother on her own.

During the closed season for diving, when his mother worked on the mainland, Azami was responsible for looking after his brother. After graduating middle school, he refused his mother's suggestion to attend high school and quickly obtained a 4th-class boat pilot license while helping with fishing around the island. He is now able to take his father's small fishing boat, the Saiun-Maru, out on fishing trips on his own.

He has a frank, easygoing relationship with Yuza, his childhood friend, and the two often get up to mischief together. Although he was happy for Yuza when he left to attend high school on the mainland and later found a job there, he also felt somewhat lonely. For this reason, he secretly welcomed the news that Yuza would be leaving his job and returning to Kameshima to take care of his grandmother.
From in-game profile
Sex: Female
Occupation: Exchange Student; Exorcist
Age: 15 years old

A young exorcist from England, currently on exchange in Japan. Possessed of a bold and willful nature, she harbors an ardent interest in Japanese folklore and occult stories. She is quick to involve herself in anything that interests her, not stopping until her curiosity has been completely sated. Although she can be fairly blunt, she shows a naivety appropriate to her age around those she's comfortable with, and is not above the occasional prank.

Circe is the third daughter of Ciara Lunarlight, the current head of the matrilineal Lunarlight family, a long line of exorcists based in England. Along with her two older sisters, she has received a specialized education in exorcism ever since she was a child, and is currently in training as an apprentice.

As the beings known as "demons" in the West ultimately share the same root cause as harmful supernatural phenomena in the East —the spirits of the dead, strong thoughts, and curses— what she does as an exorcist is fundamentally the same as what Japanese psychics do, with only the methods and terminology differing.

Although she is supposed to be in the care of the Paranormal Affairs Bureau —a confidential Japanese institute— during her time in Japan, Circe has been spending more time traveling around the country sightseeing than working through her training curriculum. The supervisor in charge of her training has all but given up on trying to manage her as a result, resolving to keep an eye on her but otherwise not interfere; as such, she's afforded a relatively high level of freedom.

Circe is an ardent fan of Mio Kurosuzu, a girl with potent spirit sense and her senior in the industry in Japan. She harbors both strong admiration and strong feelings of rivalry towards her in equal measure, and it is not uncommon for her to end up a babbling mess when then topic turns to the other girl. She treasures the photograph she had taken with Mio upon first meeting her in Tokyo, and keeps it with her at all times.

A man who visited Kameshima alongside Yumeko Shiki.

An independent psychic who makes his living as Japan's only "psychic detective." Sodo has no permanent residence, instead traveling throughout the country for training and resolving any metaphysical incidents he comes across — something which eventually led to him gaining his current moniker within the industry. Although he has a calm and taciturn personality and is possessed of a sharp mind, he is surprisingly sensitive by nature; however, this trait does not extend to mercy towards spirits and other phenomena, which he often ends up subduing by force.

Sodo's family runs a small shrine dedicated to a certain onmyoji from the Sengoku period. This onmyoji is said to be an ancestor of the Kiryu family, which may explain why their bloodline has produced many individuals with a strong spirit sense over the years.

Sodo was born with an exceptionally potent spirit sense even within his lineage, leading to his abilities catching the attention of legendary psychic Ittensai Shiki when he was eight years old. Ittensai subsequently took him under his wing as his protégé, and Sodo underwent rigorous training under his watchful eye.
From in-game profile
Sex: Female
Occupation: High School Student; Apprentice Ama Diver
Age: 17 years old
A girl born and raised in Kameshima. She has a bright, friendly nature and an inquisitive personality. Currently in her second year of high school, she boasts excellent grades and a sharp intuition.

She has been staying at a relative's house in Ise City since last year in order to attend an all-girl's high school on the mainland, and is currently back on Kameshima for summer break. Despite this, she frequently makes trips back to the island on weekends, and has been trying her hand at underwater gathering since the current diving season began, having long been interested in the ama lifestyle. Her estimated Diver Rank is 6. However, her teachers have been strongly encouraging her to aim for a national university.

She has been friends with Azami Kumoi and Yuza Minakuchi since childhood, with their close rapport making up for their difference in academic years, and it was more common to find her playing with the two boys than with girls her own age up until middle school. However, since leaving the island to attend high school, she has grown more conscious of their age difference, and has put some distance between herself and them.

She hit it off immediately with Sato Shiranami, a girl who came to Kameshima to lodge with the Wakamuras a few months ago, and was looking forward to showing her around the island and helping her adapt to life there whenever she returns home.

18 years ago, her still pregnant mother, Nagisa Awao, moved to Kameshima alone before giving birth to Tsukasa shortly afterwards. Tsukasa subsequently grew up in a single-mother household. Although she used to occasionally ask her mother about her father, her questions were always evaded, so she has since stopped inquiring. However, the fact that her mother never seems to have any financial difficulty despite not working has led her to quietly suspect he might still be involved in some way.

In truth, Tsukasa secretly tracked down her father —a wealthy man who owns multiple companies in Ise— and knows that she is his illegitimate child. She has apparently even gone out to dinner with him several times, but keeps this a secret from her mother.

Occupation: Prefectural Police Detective
Age: 35

An assistant inspector in the First Investigative Division of the Criminal Investigation Department of the Mie Prefectural Police. He often finds himself saddled with whatever troublesome tasks come to the department's way —something he makes sure to grumble about each time— but is a proficient detective in his own right, being diligent in his duties and having passed his promotion exam without difficulty.
Although often said to have a somewhat unreadable expression, he is quite sociable and makes a point to attend all the department drinking parties.

Born and raised in Mie, Masaru never ventured beyond bicycle commuting distance of his hometown, Tsu City, until the time came for him to attend university. With no particular plans for his future in mind, he took the employment exam for police officers, figuring that a local government job would at least be stable. He had no admiration for the police or any strong sense of duty or justice, but found the strict discipline of the police force suited his personality.

He quietly married a fellow classmate from the police academy soon after graduating, and at home he takes on the role of doting father to two sons and a daughter. If pressed to discuss his hobbies, they would include walking and combination puzzles. Strangely enough, he often happens to be walking nearby whenever incidents occur, leading to him being first on the scene even when off duty — something his colleagues frequently tease him about.
From in-game profile
Sex: Male
Occupation: Event Services Co. CEO
Age: 26 years old

Director of Sala Planning, a venture company primarily focused on planning and producing tourism promotion events in Ise City. An ambitious young man, Kippei is both highly driven and extraordinarily tenacious when it comes to fulfilling his goals. He is currently planning a PR project themed on "mermaids" as a sightseeing attraction.

About six years ago, with the support of wealthy tycoon Yoshiatsu Yamashina, Kippei moved to Ise from the countryside with nothing but the clothes on his back and an eye to making his fortune. This aggressiveness won him Yamashina's favor, and after several years spent building up experience as his assistant, the tycoon granted Kippei an investment with which he started his current company. Although Yamashina could be said to be particularly strict with him, this is a reflection of the high expectations he has for his future.
Kippei is often told that he looks old for his age, but as this means he is not taken lightly when doing business, he sees it as an advantage.
His true identity is Taira no Tomoshige, a member of the Heike who gained immortality 800 years ago. He once also went by the name Komatsu Sadamune during the Sengoku period.

Approximately six years ago, he murdered a youth by the name of Kippei Ikoma and assumed his identity before approaching Yoshiatsu Yamashina in a bid to wile his way into his trust — a strategy he has used multiple times before with other influential figures. Once he had gained it, he planted the idea of attaining immortality in his mind and encouraged him to begin searching for mermaids.

However, a careless comment by Shinobu Wakamura revealed that Osato —a girl Tomoshige had been close to during the height of the Heike's power— had also become an 800-year immortal and was currently living on Kameshima.

Tomoshige felt a sudden, intense longing for that long-lost time, and in that instant his ambitions seemed to lose all meaning. Nearing the end of his life and beginning to feel a growing sense of futility at his failure to fulfill his goals, he perhaps wished that someone who knew him would recognize his solitary struggle and show appreciation for his efforts. Feeling that this chance at reunion must be fate, he became singularly fixated on the idea of finding Osato and reaching the end of his life together with her.

To that end, he conferred his curse stone to Kikuko Tsutsui, who he had stationed on Kameshima to monitor the sacred sanctuary, and tried to threaten Osato into giving herself up. However, when he lost contact with Kikuko, he realized that his plan had failed, and, with the end of his lifespan drawing near, decided to head to Kameshima himself.

Fortunately, he had secretly been supporting those who sought to lift the Curse of the Raging Waves, and the culmination of their efforts saw the curse broken at last. However, at the time of its dispelling, Tomoshige found himself confined to a cell in the Yamashina estate.

Yoshiatsu, whose patience with him had worn thin due to the increasing selfishness of his actions —including his abandonment of his search for mermaids and the tamatebako— had decided to punish him for his insubordination. This would prove insufficient to stop Tomoshige. Sensing that the curse had been broken and desperate to reach Kameshima, he used his curse to kill Yoshiatsu without hesitation, having placed the symbol it used as a target throughout the mansion in advance.

Upon reaching Kameshima, he headed straight for the Wakamura residence, making sure to hand out his business card to any islanders he encountered on the way. After handing his business card to Shinobu with a pleasant smile, he pressed him to hand over Osato without delay, before using his curse to kill him on the spot upon his refusal.
Feeling the end of his lifespan fast approaching, only one thing mattered to Tomoshige now: finding Osato and fulfilling his desire to die together with her.

The only son of Shinobu Wakamura, a local Kameshima magnate. Due to his father's influence, he was pampered by those around him from an early age, but he grew up to be a pleasant and sincere young man despite this attention. He is well regarded by those who know him, often being told that he has been blessed with a sharp intellect, good looks, and a variety of talents. He is currently attending a university in Tokyo, and is back on Kameshima for summer break.

Although his father Shinobu wants Shotaro to inherit the influence and wealth he has spent much of his life building up, Shotaro himself has no intention of doing so. On the contrary, he is skeptical of the old-fashioned, insular ways of island society, and regards his father as the very embodiment of those outdated mores, viewing him with utter disgust for his overbearing, vulgar tendencies and superstitious beliefs.
From in-game profile
Sex: Male
Occupation: Local Magnate
Age: 55 years old

The single most influential person on Kameshima. Although born to an ordinary fishing family on the island, he entered his twenties during the post-war economic boom, and through tireless work and juggling multiple side jobs, he managed to amass a small fortune over the years. He went on to invest this fortune into the development of Kameshima, not only upgrading its fishing equipment, but also improving the island's infrastructure to entice business to set up shop on the island — efforts that have earned him the appreciation of people all over the island.

He currently holds many key positions on the island, including serving as head of the Kameshima Fisheries Cooperative Association, and it is said that his appointment as the next mayor of Kameshima is all but confirmed.

Although admired for his many contributions to Kameshima's development, his personality leaves much to be desired. With many stories of him using force to get things to go his way, he is often high-handed in his dealings with others, fully aware that his position makes it difficult to oppose him.

Having moved his main home and base of operations to the mainland many years prior, there are abundant rumors that he has since added loan-sharking and land grabbing to the list of ways he's willing to add to his sizable fortune.
It is said that he has recently become an ardent devotee of a certain famous sorcerer in Tokyo, and often relies on their guidance when making decisions.
From in-game profile
Sex: Female
Occupation: Veteran Ama Diver
Age: 59 years old
The de facto leader of the ama divers on Kameshima, she is a highly influential figure on the island.

She married into a family on Kameshima shortly after the end of the Second World War at the age of 20 and has been working as an ama diver for close to 40 years, rarely missing the opening day of each diving season.

She has displayed a natural talent for diving ever since her days as an apprentice, coming to be known as "Chie the Mermaid" for the deft ease in which she moves through the water. In her heyday, she earned more money than her husband — enough to send all three of her sons to university, an achievement that she takes great pride in and also earned her considerable authority in her household.

Now a grandmother to seven, a back injury has led to her being less active than she used to be, but she is still considered one of the most experienced divers on the island. Her graceful swimming shows no signs of decline, continuing to inspire others even now. Her estimated Diver Rank is 67.
From in-game profile
Sex: Female
Occupation: Housewife
Age: 63 years old

Yuza Minakuchi's paternal grandmother, and a former ama diver. Born in the Taisho period. She has a relaxed and broad-minded nature, but her tendency not to concern herself with the finer details often makes those around her uneasy.

Although now retired due to health issues, she was one of the best ama divers on Kameshima — especially in her younger days, during which she had a fierce rivalry with Chie Toyama, also know as Chie the Mermaid. Later years saw them reconcile, and they could often be seen talking and laughing together at the diver's hut while grilling their catches.
She lost her husband in the war when her son, Tosuke Minakuchi, was 3 years old.
From in-game profile
Sex: Female
Occupation: Ama Diver
Age: 28 years old

A woman born and raised on Kameshima. Unmarried. She is known for her friendly, sociable nature and almost sisterly tendency to look after others, both of which make her a familiar face to many on the island.

Ever since her school days, Kikuko harbored a strong desire to leave Kameshima and make a life for herself elsewhere. While most of her classmates began working as ama divers following graduation from middle school, she decided to enroll in a boarding school as a first step towards fulfilling this goal, going on to graduate from a junior college in Aichi Prefecture and then finding a job in general administration at a company in Ise City.

However, because her assigned work consisted only of unfulfilling, menial tasks like pouring tea and answering calls, she left after only one year. She changed jobs repeatedly over the following years, but found no further luck in subsequent workplaces. Eventually, recognizing that success as an ama diver is determined solely by the extent of one's physical prowess and ingenuity, she came to find the idea of such work appealing, and moved back to Kameshima four years ago.

Despite her late start as an ama diver compared to her peers, she leveraged her high athletic ability —a talent which even saw her star in the National Athletic Meet during her school days— and her innate knack for analytical thinking and research to consistently turn out good results, and she has since earned the respect of even the veteran ama divers of the island. Her estimated Diver Rank is 41.

Kikuko has had scant luck with men, having been introduced to several potential partners only to be turned down by all of them. Her parents, anxious for her future, worry that the large birthmark on her face is to blame, but Kikuko herself remains unfazed, citing her lack of interest in marriage as the primary cause — something which has caused them no end of concern. Although she endeavored to hide her birthmark with makeup while at school and during her time as an office worker, she has since embraced it, proudly proclaiming it to be her symbol.

While aimlessly drifting from job to job unable to find something she wanted to do, Kikuko happened to meet Kippei Ikoma, who was the president of one of the companies she ended up working for. It was then that Kippei revealed a surprising secret to her: Kikuko was in fact the illegitimate child of a wealthy tycoon, one Yoshiatsu Yamashina, and had been entrusted to a childless couple to raise as their own. Kikuko had always believed herself special in some way, and learning that she was originally of high birth only served to validate that belief, leading to her developing a strong sense of pride.

Upon learning of Kikuko's background and taking note of her dissatisfaction with her current lot in life, Kippei opted to try and make her his pawn by skillfully manipulating her sense of self-importance. His endeavors paid off: tired of what she perceived as a stifling, monotonous life and driven by both her admiration for Kippei and desire to be recognized by Yoshiatsu so she could live the life she believed she deserved, Kikuko agreed to return to Kameshima and act as his agent there.

Fueled by her ambition and exhilarated by the sense that she had become the star of one of the spy movies that had been so popular in her childhood, Kikuko's mind was set — she no longer cared if people died or her hometown was destroyed as long as it meant she could fulfill her goals.
From in-game profile
She is one of the curse bearers of The Curse of the Heike, bearing the curse stone given to her by Kippei.
Sex: Female
Occupation: Yuza's Mother
Age: Unknown
Yuza Minakuchi's mother. Having gone missing in the Kameshima Southern Sea Disaster five years ago, she was declared dead a year later after search parties found no sign of her.

More than twenty years ago, Mare Somekawa arrived on Kameishma with no possessions to her name, expressing that she had taken a liking to the local environment and wanted to move there. However, she remained tight-lipped about her background, only revealing that she was from a small town out in the mountains and that she had had to leave her home for undisclosed reasons, and although her request to move to Kameshima was accepted, many islanders remained suspicious of her.

After settling on the island, she showed an interest in the ama lifestyle and eventually took it up after displaying a talent for free-diving, with Tsuyu Minakuchi acting as her instructor. During this time, she grew close to Tosuke Minakuchi, Tsuyu's only son, and eventually married him a few years later. The two would go on to have a son of their own, who they named Yuza.

Despite this, Mare was unable to fully shake the air of mystery that surrounded her, and many islanders continued to question whether her presence on the island might cause trouble down the line. Something of a free spirit, her nonconformist ways and somewhat naive personality meant that she was often absent from local activities, leading to further criticism from a portion of the population. Some also reported frequently spotting her wandering the island after she first moved there, seemingly looking for something, or catching sight of her doing something on the shore in the middle of the night.

Fortunately, her mother-in-law, Tsuyu Minakuchi, was a person of no small influence on Kameshima, and no one dared openly persecute Mare under Tsuyu's watchful eye. The three generations lived peacefully under the same roof for more than ten years, until the Kameshima Southern Sea Disaster tore them apart.

Since her disappearance in the disaster five years prior, a growing number of people have accused her of somehow being responsible, citing her various instances of suspicious behavior as justification.
From in-game profile

Mare and her younger sister Azusa were descendants of the sole survivor of Taishima. Following the destruction of Taishima, the Somekawa line hid themselves away, living for generations in a small village within the city of Shima.
Azusa left her hometown behind, leaving the family duty to be handled by Mare alone.

The mermaid Sobae made contact with Mare, who treated her in a friendly manner from the moment of their meeting and promised to do all she could to return her to Ryugu. There was no pretense in Mare's bearing, and her attitude when speaking to Sobae was casual and lighthearted.
A strange sense of trust came to blossom between them, one transcending the boundaries of their respective species.

Mare had originally resolved to remain single and never start a family of her own in order to devote herself entirely to her duty with Sobae. However, Sobae strongly opposed this, saying that Mare's life here would continue even when she was gone, so Mare should not deny herself a possible future with her own family. Mare seemed unbothered at the thought, but said that she would consider it if someone suitable ended up coming along.
However, that moment came sooner than expected: upon moving to Kameshima, she met the love of her life, Tosuke Minakuchi.
It was Mare's constant wish to be able to introduce her beloved family to her dearest friend. Sobae said she would meet them when the time came for her to return to Ryugu.
On the day of the Southern Sea Disaster, Mare took Tosuke and Yuza out into the bay on a boat to introduce them to Sobae as promised.
The storm suddenly broke out around them, and their small fishing boat started to sink. The couple had fitted Yuza with a life boy and gotten him off the boat.
Mare and Tosuke pleaded for Sobae to help Yuza, saying that his survival meant more to them than anything else.
Smiling as she clung to the sinking boat, half-submerged in seawater, Mare thanked Sobae for her friendship and told her that the days they had spent together had been some of her happiest.

After carrying Yuza out of the reach of the storm, Sobae immediately went to rescue Mare. She finally found her after three long days of searching, but her efforts had been in vain — Mare's body was already cold.
Edited from Sobae and Azusa's in-game profiles
A wealthy tycoon who owns multiple companies and swathes of land, particularly in the Tsu and Ise areas. Born in the Taisho period. Unmarried.

His family first came into business in the Edo period, traveling from town to town selling talismans, miscanthus reed hoops, and other items to ward off evil spirits. During the Meiji period, this business expanded into a trading company, and the Yamashina family became prominent contributors to the development of the region.

Born to the heir of the Yamashina family business and the daughter of a noble family, Yoshiatsu grew up in an affluent environment, where he received a thorough education tailored to gifted children. Following the end of the war, Yoshiatsu inherited the company assets in his thirties, but was quick to sell off all the shares he owned, using the proceeds to buy and sell real estate and stocks — a practice that made him extremely wealthy.

After amassing his fortune, he showed a keen interest in investing in ambitious young people, actively mentoring those he took a particular liking to. This approach led to the emergence of many successful businessmen, which included Shinobu Wakamura of Kameshima. Those who have received Yamashina's support view him with both gratitude and a sense of awe bordering on reverence, referring to him as "Unkakudono," a title that evokes a figure elevated above the clouds.

Yamashina has always shown a strong attachment to wealth, even going so far as to partake in illicit activities such as illegal donations, tax evasion, insider trading, and media control, all in an effort to garner ever more status and money. In the shadow of the many success stories enabled by his support, many more of his beneficiaries have fallen into bankruptcy or been arrested, fueling endless unsavory rumors about him to this day. Yamashina himself, however, seems to be unconcerned by these rumors, considering anything that does not directly harm him to be beneath his notice.

Even as a lifelong bachelor, he has surrounded himself with many followers, both publicly and privately, and has never lacked for anything to satisfy his personal needs. A few years ago, he began to seriously consider the issue of a successor, driven by his determination that his beloved fortune should never fall into the hands of someone untrustworthy. Perhaps for this reason, he began to develop a keen fascination with immortality around the same time, and is said to be secretly investing vast amounts of money into research on the topic.
From in-game profile

A woman living in Toba. Although she occasionally does work as an ama diver, it is unclear who she is and where she came from. She apparently showed up in Toba about five years ago with nothing but a grubby wooden box to her name, and has been living there ever since.

As Mare Minakuchi's younger sister, Azusa is also descendant of the sole survivor of Taishima. Following the destruction of Taishima, the Somekawa line hid themselves away, living for generations in a small village within the city of Shima.

The book "The Little Mermaid" was a constant fixture in the household —a decision made so that the children of the family would grow up with a familiarity with mermaids— and Azusa read it repeatedly as she grew up, the tale fueling a fervent admiration for mermaids within her. Upon realizing that she could never be a mermaid herself, she instead decided to become an ama diver, thinking that it would at least allow her swim freely through the sea like the beings she so admired.
Thus resolved, she left her hometown behind, leaving the family duty —nothing more than a troublesome burden to Azusa— to be handled by her elder sister alone.

For all intents and purposes, it appeared that Azusa's wish had been granted. However, upon returning home following her parents' deaths, she was taken aback to learn that the family duty inherited by Mare was in itself deeply connected to mermaids. Forgetting how she had pushed the duty onto Mare to follow her own desires, Azusa grew deeply resentful of her sister, accusing her of keeping the mermaid to herself and asserting her right to take up the family duty, but it was too late. Mare and the mermaid had already forged an unbreakable bond that no amount of words or deeds could undo.

Following Mare's death, she was finally able to meet the being that had enchanted her for so long. However, her desperate plea for the mermaid to take her back to Ryugu with her was met with staunch refusal, and the mermaid left shortly after, never to return.
With her opportunity to fulfill the family duty gone and her chance at connecting with mermaids lost, Azusa sank into despondency, spending her days in an empty haze.

Amidst this despair, the Curse of the Forsaken Fish that appeared before her seemed to be a final chance to have her wish granted. Driven by regret over what she perceived as a life of wrong choices and consumed by her obsession, she threw herself into Ise Bay and surrendered herself to the curse, ultimately dying due to its effects. Her form, writhing in the agony brought on by her sudden transformation, bore no resemblance to the mermaids she had once so admired as a child, yet it is said that the expression on her face when her body was discovered a day later in Futamigaura seemed somehow content.

A mysterious sorcerer. Although said to possess exceptional supernatural abilities, they have revealed nothing of their true identity. Both their age and gender are unknown.
As of The Seven Mysteries of Honjo

Suigen Gamyodo was previously most known for their prominent media presence, with numerous appearances both on television and in magazines. Wearing an unusual outfit that covered their face, they would demonstrate a variety of psychic abilities, including exorcism of possessed individuals, assessment of submitted ghost photographs, identification of guiding spirits, and conduction of telepathic readings at haunted locations. Their unique sense of presence and high rate of accuracy garnered them a sizable following, particularly among occult enthusiasts, and they were known to accept consultations from the general public as well as media outlets.
As of The Mermaid's Curse

However, the end of the previous year saw this once public figure suddenly withdraw from the spotlight. They now mainly operate behind closed doors, signing consulting agreements with particular companies to provide a variety of services, including management advice from a metaphysical perspective, divination of auspicious and harmful events, proposals to improve their clients' luck, and the detection and elimination of paranormal disturbances. It is rumored that they will even cast curses on key personnel at rival companies, or conversely exorcise curses from targeted victims, for the right price.

The undeniable potency of their spiritual abilities has earned them immense trust from both the executives of their contracted companies and other wealthy individuals, and their behind-the-scenes reputation continues to grow. This has resulted in a sharp rise in their consulting fees, placing their services far beyond what any average individual can reasonably hope to afford. One of the companies they currently have a contract with belongs to Shinobu Wakamura, a local Kameshima magnate.

Among psychics, opinion on them is more divided. Many have noted that their spiritual ability during the time they were openly active in the media was too weak to allow them to perform advanced techniques of any sort —to the extent that they were considered little better than a fraud— leading to suspicions about what prompted their sudden change in course.

It is now almost impossible to find footage and articles from their past media appearances, and the names of the companies with which they have consulting contracts are entirely undisclosed, obfuscating their identity, purpose, and the true extent of their power.
From profile in The Mermaid's Curse

According to the results of an investigation conducted by the Paranormal Affairs Bureau, the original Suigen Gamyodo retired following last year's incident involving the Seven Mysteries of Honjo, and a young man with exceptionally potent spirit sense has since taken her place.

Although this second Suigen Gamyodo has thus far focused on using his powerful abilities to solidify his social standing, his true purpose seems to be searching for a diviner by the name of Iyo Tokoro, who is said to be responsible for teaching the art of curses and other supernatural techniques to a certain ordinary woman.
From in-game files
The curse echo of The Curse of the Heike/The Curse of Taira no Tomoshige.
Curse:
Uses a specific symbol as its target, and kills those who carry that symbol within the area specified by the user by cleaving them in two. Its effective range is several hundred meters.
Its curse bearer is
Taira no Tomoshige himself, naturally wielding the curse. A curse stone with this curse was conferred to Kikuko Tsutsui.

A curse born from Taira no Tomoshige's feelings of malice and resentment when he was struck down 800 years ago following the fall of the Taira clan. Part of the clan's main lineage, Tomoshige had been seeking a mermaid flesh in a bid to attain immortally with the goal of eventually reviving the Taira clan, but was killed before realizing his dream.

Taira no Tomoshige was born as the son of Taira no Kiyomori's younger brother, Yorimori, in the latter half of the Heian period at the height of the Taira clan's power. Although his father Yorimori was the only child born of the official wife of Taira no Tadamori —part of the main lineage of the Taira clan— he maintained a deferential attitude towards Kiyomori, a stance that made Tomoshige regard him with contempt and fueled his ambition to one day stand at the head of the Taira clan.

In 1185, the Taira clan was defeated at the Battle of Dan-no-ura, spelling its ruin. Tomoshige, who had fled from place to place as if to desperately avert his eyes from the Taira clan's decline, ultimately did not participate in the decisive battle at Dan-no-ura, and came to know of the Taira clan's downfall while he was lying low in a remote village in Ise with the imperial maidservant Sato.

Tomoshige continued to search for a way to turn the situation to his advantage. In the process, he suddenly remembered a box that his grandfather Tadamori had left the family — a tamatebako proffered by a fisherman that was said to contain the flesh of a mermaid.

Tomoshige located the tamatebako and pried open the lid. However, all that was inside was a dried sliver of meat, so shriveled as to resemble a splint of wood. Dubios, Tomoshige pushed his misgivings aside and ate the meat, but felt no different than before. Believing that long years had robbed the meat of its power, and seeing the tamatebako as his only clue to find a mermaid, he boarded a small boat with Sato and set out to sea.

Their small boat was surrounded by ships belonging to a small band hunting down remnants of the Taira clan. Alarmed, they tried to flee, but with their attackers pressing in on them from all sides, were unable to find any means of escape.

Tomoshige, still determined to retaliate, continued to frantically resist with his sword. However, he was vastly outnumbered, and, unable to break through his attackers' ranks, was ultimately cut down in a single stroke.

On the brink of death, Tomoshige's gaze fell on the crests worn by his pursuers. Consumed by bitter regret at his failure to restore his clan, he directed the full brunt of his resentment towards these symbols as he sank beneath the waves, cursing his enemies and clinging to his vindictive hatred until the very end.
Edited from in-game Files
In truth, Tomoshige successfully gained immortal and survived the attack. He lives in the modern age under the name Kippei Ikoma.

Tomoshige had spent the past 800 years working alone in the shadows, possessed by the single desire of restoring the Heike. His plan has remained unchanged: obtain wealth and status, gain the power of immortality, build up an immortal army, and rise to power through force.

He perhaps came closest to this goal during the Sengoku era, where —as Komatsu Sadamune, a vassal of the Kuki clan— he managed to invade Taishima, an island said to be the dwelling place of mermaids, but this attempt ultimately ended in failure. Refusing to give up, he continued to devise various schemes after that in pursuit of his goal, but none of them met with success.

As the modern age approached, his accumulated resentment eventually grew so strong that he gained the ability to wield it as a curse. Since attaining his power, he has sought out young men with no family of a similar age to him and used it to kill them without leaving any evidence, before going on to assume their identity. He disposed of all their bodies at a. point in the sea near Toba where the currents happened to stagnate — the perfect spot to ensure they would remain undiscovered.
Edited from "Kippei Ikoma"'s in-game profile
The curse echo of The Curse of the Forsaken Fish.
Curse: Kills any human submerged in the waters of Ise Bay by gradually turning them into a fish starting from their feet.
Its curse bearer is Arnav Barnum.
A curse born from the final moments of Hayase, a mermaid brutally tortured to death by humans on Taishima around 400 years ago.
The excruciating pain suffered during the transformation often results in the victim dying before the metamorphosis is complete.

The bodies of those who succumb to the curse decay almost instantly, shriveling up into desiccated, fibrous masses. The curse can also be triggered remotely, provided that the curse bearer knows their victim's exact location.

Mermaids inherently possess the ability to turn humans into fish at will. The Curse of the Forsaken Fish is the result of that ability being turned into a conditional curse and sealed within a curse stone.
During the Invasion of Taishima, Hayase stayed behind on the island as bait to allow Sobae, Nagame, Princess Hatsune, and a man named Somekawa to escape.

Komatsu Sadamune's forces discovered Hayase in hiding and captured her. Sadamunde demanded that she make his troops immortal, but the mermaid staunchly refused — even as Sadamune turned to torture, inflicting unspeakable pain with every refusal. The torture escalated, until eventually even her supernatural nature was not enough to withstand the torment.
On the brink of death and resigned to her fate, Hayase gave a final terrible cry, overflowing with resentment and anger as she breathed her last.

Sadamune ordered his men to take the flesh from her body, but as they moved to do so, a strange phenomenon began to occur — all the soldiers who approached her body began to transform into fish, their bodies decaying rapidly as the transformation took hold. Hayase had cast a curse upon them with her dying breath.

The two remaining mermaids — Nagame and Sobae— were left unable to return home. Nagame seized the opportunity to travel the world, a journey that would span the next 400 years. The more serious Sobae was deeply affected by Hayase's sacrifice; mourning her loss and filled with longing to return home to Ryugu, she spent her days hidden in the depths of Ise Bay, weeping bitterly.
Edited from in-game Files

One of the three mermaids who were said to have lived near Taishima about 400 years ago. She has since returned to her home, Ryugu.

After becoming unable to return to Ryugu, Sobae had ceased to show herself on the surface, even before members of the Somekawa line. However, upon noticing that they were approaching 400 years since the sinking of Taishima, she cautiously attempted contact with the current generation's inheritor of the family duty — a woman by the name of Mare Somekawa.

Gradually, Sobae began to open up to her. After some time, they agreed on a secret signal and began meeting surreptitiously, growing closer the more they learned about each other. A strange sense of trust came to blossom between them, one transcending the boundaries of their respective species.

Mare had originally resolved to remain single and never start a family of her own in order to devote herself entirely to her duty with Sobae. However, Sobae strongly opposed this, saying that Mare's life here would continue even when she was gone, so Mare should not deny herself a possible future with her own family. She had seen how happy one of her former compatriots had been upon finding love, and believed Mare deserved to know such joy as well if she wished to.
Once Mare met the love of her life, Tosuke Minakuchi, Sobae was delighted for her, and offered her heartfelt congratulations upon hearing of their marriage.
In the days leading up to the Southern Sea Disaster, Sobae and Mare mistakenly concluded that the seal the Curse of the Raging Waves and to Rouge's entrance would soon be lifted.
The storm suddenly broke out, and Sobae immediately rushed to the Minakuchi's aid, reaching them just as they had fitted Yuza with a life buoy and gotten him off the boat.
Frantic, she tried to take only Mare with her in a bid to escape the sinking boat, but Mare rebuffed her attempt. Instead, she and Tosuke pleaded for Sobae to help Yuza.
Deep down, part of Sobae resented Yuza and Tosuke with all her being.
Wrenching herself away from the sinking boat, Sobae headed to rescue Yuza, all the while resenting the boy for the tremendous love that Mare bore him.
When she found Yuza, he had been caught up in a whirlpool and has barely clinging to life.

The next moment, she dragged the dying Yuza out of the whirlpool and, pulling a piece off her won tail, forcibly fed it to him. Whether the emotions driving her at this point were a desire to fulfill Mare's wish or hatred towards Yuza, even Sobae herself couldn't say.

After carrying Yuza out of the reach of the storm, Sobae immediately went to rescue Mare. She finally found her after three long days of searching, but her efforts had been in vain — Mare's body was already cold.
Sobae clung to Mare's body and wept. She laid Mare's body to rest on the seabed, and, hiding herself beside it, spent her days mourning, lost in the depths of despair.

Several years later, the entrance to Ryugu was unsealed, and Sobae —now with no remaining attachments to the mortal world— made to return home by herself. Before doing so, she met with Mare's sister, thinking to reclaim the mermaids' relic from her. However, put off by the woman's blatant avarice, she found herself unable to muster any interest in her, and ultimately returned without reclaiming the relic despite knowing full well the misfortune it could bring.
Edited from in-game profile
On August 7, while Yuza Minakuchi was diving, he encountered a being that looked exactly like himself. Azami wondered if this might be the "Tomokazuki" from a ghost story told among divers.

In truth, it is actually Yuza Minakuchi's consciousness, split from his immortal body when his head was decapitated during the Tragedy of Kameshima. As a spirit, it serves as the Player Insert Character for the story.

This separate consciousness found a way to Ryugu, a place that lies on the boundary of dimensions. As a spirit, it possessed Yuza and others, then traveled across time and space in attempt to guide the course of the story.
Yumeko Shiki's husband and a psychic. Sodo Kiryu is his cherished protégé.

About fifty years ago, Nagame met a certain talented psychic in Japan. The two quickly fell in love, and Nagame —who by that point had begun to earnestly wish that she could give up being a mermaid and live among humans in the mortal world— asked him whether there was any way she could become human. Wanting to fulfill her wish, the psychic began to search for a lost secret art that would allow her to assume human form. The two overcame countless hardships together in their quest for the art, and after decades of searching, they not only found it but finally succeeded in perfecting it.

However, the secret art that would grant Nagame her wish demanded a heavy price: for a mermaid —a being who lacked a mortal form in the material world— to gain a human body, the caster's own body would have to be sacrificed. Using this art would render them unable to live side-by-side as humans as they had so longed to do.

The two agonized over their decision. Despite their decades-long search, the different worlds in which they lived continued to keep them apart —as a mermaid, Nagame could neither join him on land nor appear before others. The life together they yearned for remained a distant dream.

In the end, the two chose to use the secret art so they could be together in the mortal world. Even when Nagame learned that the psychic, Ittensai Shiki, only appeared young due to his supernatural abilities —having been born in the Edo period and already over a hundred years old by that time— she loved him no less.

After many twists and turns in their quest for happiness, the spirit of Ittensai Shiki, who sacrificed his body so that Yumeko could live as a human, has come to dwell in the body of a small dog, and he continues to enjoy retirement and a quiet life at Yumeko's side in his home in Tokyo to this day.

Even before his retirement (and despite his current form), he remained an active force in the industry, having devoted his time to such things as taking Sodo Kiryu on as his protégé after discovering his potential, assisting with management of the Paranormal Affairs Bureau for old times' sake, and sending Yumeko —who knew of the Bureau and the work it did— to help out as one of its members.
Edited from Yumeko Shiki's in-game profile

segments.text: The current head of the matrilineal Lunarlight family, a long line of exorcists based in England. She has given a specialized education in exorcism to her three duaghters, with Circe currently in training as an apprentice.
Edited from Circe Lunarlight's in-game profile
Tsukasa Awao mother.

18 years ago, a still-pregnant Nagisa moved to Kameshima alone before giving birth to Tsukasa shortly afterwards. Tsukasa subsequently grew up in a single-mother household. Although Tsukasa used to occasionally ask her about her father, she always evaded her questions, so Tsukasa has since stopped inquiring. However, the fact that Nagisa never seems to have any financial difficulty despite not working has led Tsukasa to quietly suspect that he might still be involved in some way.
Edited from Tsukasa Awao's in-game profile
Nagisa used to work as a maid for Yoshiatsu Yamashina, Tsukasa's biological father. Nagisa shares hostility towards Yamashina, but still receives financial support from him.
Azami Kumoi's father.
Captain of the fishing vessel Dai-ichi Kyosui-Maru. He was among the 10 casualties of the Southern Sea Disaster after his vessel was foundered.

A fisherman who frequently had Azami accompany him out to sea on his boat from a very young age. As a result, Azami grew up never doubting that he, too, would one day become a fisherman. After Kyokichi died, his wife —an ama diver— took on the responsibility of raising Azami and his much younger brother on her own.
Azami is now able to take his father's small fishing boat, the Saiun-Maru, out on fishing trips on his own.
Edited from in-game files and Azami Kumoi's in-game profile

The tale of Yao Bikuni —a bhikkhuni (fully-ordained Buddhist nun) who acquired preternatural longevity after eating the flesh of a mermaid— can be found in almost every region of Japan. Although the exact details vary greatly between regions they all share the same fundamental element: a girl who ate mermaid flesh lived for 800 years.
The Yao Bikuni legend passed down in Mie Prefecture is as follows:

Once upon time, a beautiful girl by the name of Osato lived in Kusawa Village. One day, when Osato was seventeen, the flesh of a mermaid was served at a village gathering. The other villagers, disturbed at the thought of eating such a strange creature, refused to eat it, but Osato unknowingly ate the mermaid's flesh. From that moment on, Osato didn't age a day. Shunned by the other villagers and treated as a monster, she was eventually forced to leave the village. Becoming a nun, Osato traveled the length and breadth of Japan for hundreds of years before eventually returning to Kusawa Village, where her long life at last came to an end.

In the Heian period, Sato was living a simple life in Kusawa Village, the place of her birth. One day, she happened to encounter a visiting onmyoji and was offered the chance to work at the Bureau of Onmyo in Kyoto. Sato readily accepted, having always felt out of place in the village due to her faint spirit sense, and left Kusawa to work in the Bureau of Onmyo as a maidservant.

Taira no Tomoshige visited the imperial palace and encountered Sato, who was attending to odd jobs nearby. Tomoshige was intrigued by Sato, who made no attempts to curry favor with him and whose thoughts she found difficult to read, and he frequently visited her from then on. As their interactions continued, he found himself becoming particularly drawn to her. He eventually had a pair of bronze hadn't mirrors made and gifted one to her, telling her to carry it with her at all times as a sign of their vow to each other.
In 1185, the Taira clan was defeated at the Battle of Dan-no-ura, spelling it's ruin, as Tomoshige and Sato were laying low in a remote village in Ise.
Although initially terrified of being hunted down by soldiers of the Minamoto Clan, Tomoshige regained his senses upon seeing Sato's unbroken composure.
Tomoshige located the tamatebako left in the family, and seeing it as his only clue to find a mermaid, he boarded a small boat with Sato and set out to sea.

After they had rowed for a while, a sudden mist descended over the sea around them, obscuring their surroundings. As Tomoshige and Sato looked around fearfully, they heard a small splash; turning to look, the two gasped as they saw what appeared to be a human hand reach up from the water before grabbing onto the boat's edge.

Climbing into the boat, the mermaid screamed for the to give back the box before suddenly lunging at them. Tomoshige drew his sword and slashed at the mermaid, which let out a piercing cry before diving back into the water and fleeing the area.

Tomoshige caught sight of a piece of the mermaid's tail, stowing it in the tamatebako. Eventually, he forced Sato to eat it despite her protests. They waited a while, but no change seemed to come over her.
As the mist around them cleared, they realized their small boat was surrounded by ships belonging to a band hunting down remnants of the Taira clan.
Amidst the chaos, Sato was struck in the head by an arrow and fell into the sea.

After that, Kusawa Village found itself in an uproar following the return of Sato, who had been employed in the service of the Heike. However, after it was discovered that she had somehow become immortal, she was shunned by the other villagers, who found her newfound state unsettling, and she soon left the village for parts unknown.
A fragmented version of these events would go on to be passed down orally, eventually becoming one of the Yao Bikuni legends told to this day.
Edited from in-game Files
A vassal of the Kuki clan during the Sengoku period.

Komatsu Sadamune approached Kuki Yoshitaka with some intriguing information: three mermaids were said to be living on Taishima under the protection of some of the island's residents even though the island was thought to be uninhabited.
Sadamune urged Yoshitaka to take advantage of this, suggesting that if he possessed such power, and invincible army would be his to command.
Yoshitaka gave the order for Sadamune to prepare a military invasion of Taishima.
Sadamune immediately set sail for Taishima at the head of a large army. In the blink of an eye, the once peaceful and beautiful landscape of Taishima was transformed into a nightmare.

The islanders, guardians of the cared land, desperately fought back, but they stood no chance against seasoned soldiers hardened by years of battle on the frtonlines, and one after another they fell before the invaders. Sadamune ordered that even women and children be cut down without mercy, and soon the waters around Taishima ran red with blood.
Finally, they discovered a mermaid in hiding by the name of Hayase and captured her, torturing her to death.

Eventually, he found a deep cave in the interior of the island, which housed a shrine and a door with a power seal. Convinced this had to be the entrance to the "sacred land" —the home of the mermaids— Sadamune gathered all his remaining gunpowder and artillery and unleashed it on the door, destroying both it and the shrine in the process.

The next moment, a violent tremor wracked the entire island, and the skies above were engulfed by a storm. Taishima sank beneath the waves, and thus Taishima and the sacred land —along with Sadamune and his army— lost to the sea in an instant.
Sadamune was in fact Taira no Tomoshige, who had eaten mermaid flesh and gained unnatural longevity.

Unable to let go of his dream of reviving the Taira clan even after 400 years, he caught wind of rumors of mermaids being worshipped on Taishima, and infiltrated the Kuki navy under the name Komatsu Sadamune, plotting to uncover the sacred land. However, his rash and impulsive destruction of the sacred land ended up triggering the Curse of the Raging Waves, and his plan ultimately ended in failure.

Although caught up in the sinking of Taishima, Tomoshige could not die, and was swept away by the sea to an unknown fate. He never directly met Princess Hatsune, and as such the two remained unaware of each other's existence.
Edited from in-game Files

Tsuyu Minakuchi's son, Mare's husband, and Yuza's father. Captain of the fishing vessel Minakuchi-Maru. He and his wife were among the 10 casualties of the Southern Sea Disaster after his vessel was foundered.
Around twenty years ago, he grew close to Mare and eventually married her a few years later. The two would go on to have a son of their own, who they named Yuza.
The three generations lived peacefully under the same roof for more than ten years, until the Kameshima Southern Sea Disaster tore them apart.
He lost his father in the war when he was 3 years old.
Edited from Mare's profile, Tsuyu's profile, and in-game Files
The nephew of Kuki Yoshitaka.

While Yoshitaka was in the service of Nobunaga, the head of the Kuki clan was Sumitaka, with Yoshitaka serving as his advisor. Despite his position, Sumitaka was little more than a puppet lord and died young, reportedly due to illness, just two years after the Honno-ji Incident. However, some theories suggest that he was actually poisoned by Yoshitaka as part of a scheme to seize control of the family.

Sumitaka strongly opposed Yoshitaka's approach towards Taishima to capture the mermaids. It was in fact Sumitaka who had secretly been protecting the mermaids on Taishima. Believing the mermaids to be messengers of the gods and the island a sacred sanctuary, he had worked to keep them isolated from outside influence.

His adopted daughter, Princess Hatsune, was also living in hiding on Taishima at the time for other reasons, which further strengthened his opposition to Yoshitaka's plan. However, it was not long before Komatsu Sadamune learned of this. He reported to Yoshitaka that Sumitaka was not only planning to keep the mermaids for himself, but was also secretly moving to build an army of his own.

Yoshitaka gave the order for Sadamune to prepare a military invasion of Taishima. Caught off guard by the unexpected attack, Sumitaka scrambled to send out his own forces in an attempt to resist, but was unable to prevent the enemy from landing.

Following the sinking of Taishima, Sumitaka eventually made it to the seas near the island, but a fierce anger and resentment darkened the waters around it, and the curse born from these dark emotions —the Curse of the Raging Waves— had given rise to a storm that continued to rage even several days after the incident.

Sumitaka, looking for a solution, turned to Harukage Tsuchimikado, a renowned onmyoji and friend of Princess Hatsune. Harukage sealed the sacred land by offering Princess Hatsune as a sacrifice, thereby suppressing the curse's calamitous effects.

To protect the sacred land and the mermaids, Sumitaka ensured all records of Taishima were erased so no mention of the island or the disaster that had befallen it would make its way into historical accounts. He also concocted a tale in which Princess Hatsune had thrown herself down a well in defiance of a political marriage in order to conceal her sacrifice.

Afterwards, Kuki Yoshitaka, infuriated not only by his failure to obtain immortality but also by the loss of his primary military force, murdered Suimtaka —who opposed him to the very end— and seized control of the Kuki clan in both name and nature.
Edited from in-game Files

Kuki Sumitaka's daughter, Princess Hatsune, was said to have been a woman of great beauty. Sumitaka planned to marry her off as part of a political marriage; however, Princess Hatsune refused, saying that she had already promised her future to someone else. Upon learning that Princess Hatsune's beloved was a member of an enemy clan, Sumitaka was enraged and insisted that she marry the person he had chosen for her.

Although Princess Hatsune made numerous attempts to escape in order to be with her lover, she was caught each time and forced to return home. Despairing of her fate, Princess Hatsune lamented her beauty, blaming it for her predicament, before throwing herself down a well in her sorrow. As she did so, she prayed with her last breath that no beautiful women would ever be born in that land again, or so the legend goes. Despite the tale persevering as part of local folklore, many questions about the accuracy of Princess Hatsune's legend remain, including Sumitaka's age at the time.

Having eaten the flesh of a mermaid and becoming an 800-year immortal, Sato spent years wandering across Japan. Eventually, with the help of the onmyouji Harukage Tsuchimikado —a descendant of one of her former benefactors— she made her way to Taishima, an island rumored to be home to mermaids, and began to live there quietly.

The islanders, duty-bound to protect the mermaids and the entrance to Ryugu, were accepting of her and her circumstances, and Sato was finally able to fain the peaceful life she had been searching for. Having changed her name many times during her years of wandering, she was going by Hatsune at the time.

After she had spent some time there, Kuki Sumitaka —under whose jurisdiction Taishima fell— grew fond of her, and took her in as his adopted daughter. Initially unaware of her true identity, Sumitaka eventually discovered her immortality but, even so, continued to treat her the same as he always had, and Sato came to trust him as well.

Following the invasion of Taishima, Sato sacrificed herself in order to quell the Curse of the Raging Waves, with Harukage's ritual causing her to fall into a deep sleep within the sacred land at the bottom of the sea. The seal on the sacred land was set to break 400 years later, which was in fact to awaken Sato from her slumber.
Edited from in-game Files
A renowned onmyouji and friend of Princess Hatsune during the Sengoku period.
As a descendant of one of Hatsune/Sato's former benefactors, he helped her make her way to Taishima, an island rumored to be home to mermaids.

Kuki Sumitaka, looking for a solution to the Curse of the Raging Waves, turned to Harukage. After conducting an investigation, Harukage concluded that it would be possible to seal the sacred land by offering up a sacrifice, thereby suppressing its calamitous effects. With Princess Hatsune's noble sacrifice, the storm at last died down, and peace was restored to the seas around the island.
Edited from in-game Files

Harukage was also able to seal the Curse of the Forsaken Fish in the wooden accessory that Princess Hatsune had been wearing, turning it into a curse stone. Harukage used the resentful memories contained within the curse stone to create a record of the event, which he sealed within a heavily-locked iron box before concealing it in a rock on the seabed. In the event the Curse of the Raging Waves had not abated even after 400 years, he made it so that the seal on the rock would be lifted at the same time as the seal on the sacred land, so that the record of what had happened and the method of undoing the curse would make its way to future generations.
